title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-14
ranking_basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains, descending
ranking_explanation: Repositories are ranked by the stars gained shown on the official GitHub Trending daily view. Sponsored cards and one repo making difficult-to-verify gaming-performance claims were omitted. Current stars, languages, and default-branch commit SHAs were corroborated against GitHub REST; a Search API freshness query was a cross-check, not a ranking source.
global_caveat: Trending gains and total stars are live counts and may change after capture. This is a curated selection rather than a complete census; sponsored entries and one repo with difficult-to-verify claims were omitted. Daily stars measure short-window attention, not project quality or sustained adoption. No prior-window evidence was collected, so no notable shift is claimed.

themes.title: Agent guidance and review
themes.content: Modern Web Guidance supplies curated, current web-platform guidance to coding agents; OpenCodeReview combines deterministic review steps with LLM reasoning; Plannotator routes human annotations back into agent sessions.

themes.title: Browser access and agent integration
themes.content: Chrome DevTools MCP provides live browser automation and diagnostics, Qwen Code spans several interfaces, and AG-UI targets the agent-to-frontend protocol boundary.

themes.title: Workflow orchestration and domain skills
themes.content: LoopForge adds approval-gated agent delivery workflows, while Claude Trading Skills applies agents to structured market analysis and trading workflows.

themes.title: Beyond agent tooling
themes.content: Sure and Univer point to personal finance and office-productivity interest; Airgorah contributes a distinct Wi-Fi security-auditing signal.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-11-14 17:35 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-14 through 2026-11-14. Ranking basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains, ranked descending; live totals and freshness corroborated with GitHub REST/Search APIs.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-oriented developer tooling leads the day's organic momentum: modern-web guidance gained 1,225 stars, Alibaba's AI code review gained 897, and browser access, human review, and agent skills also feature prominently. Significant gains for a personal-finance app and a Wi-Fi security tool show the list extends beyond AI coding infrastructure.

sections.title: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src
sections.description: Source and evaluation toolkit for agent skills that teach current web-platform practices.
sections.content: Source and evaluation toolkit for agent skills that teach current web-platform practices.
sections.why_notable: The largest daily gain in this curated set; it delivers expert browser guidance to coding agents rather than relying on generic model recall.
sections.unique_caveat: This -src repository is the source and evaluation project; its README points end users to the separate Modern Web Guidance package and documentation.

sections.title: alibaba/open-code-review
sections.description: An AI-assisted code-review tool that combines deterministic checks with an LLM agent.
sections.content: The README describes a hybrid review system that reads diffs and wider file context, then produces structured line-level comments; it also supports whole-file scans.
sections.why_notable: It couples one of the day's strongest gains with a precision-oriented hybrid design and structured, line-level review comments.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository's benchmark and performance claims are project-reported; independent reproduction was not part of this snapshot.

sections.title: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
sections.description: MCP server and CLI that let coding agents inspect and operate a live Chrome browser.
sections.content: The README documents browser automation, debugging, network inspection, screenshots, and performance tracing through Chrome DevTools.
sections.why_notable: Its gain reflects demand for browser automation, debugging, and performance inspection inside agent workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: The README officially supports Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing and warns that the MCP client can inspect or modify browser data.

sections.title: we-promise/sure
sections.why_notable: A substantial non-AI product signal in a day otherwise led by developer tooling.

sections.title: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills
sections.description: Claude Code skills for market analysis, charting, screening, and trading workflows.
sections.content: A domain-specific set of Claude Code skills for investment and trading workflows.
sections.why_notable: It shows continued interest in applying agent skills to a specific professional domain, beyond general software development.

sections.title: dream-num/univer
sections.description: An extensible office SDK for editing, calculations, collaboration, and file processing.
sections.content: The project describes an open office SDK for embedding editing, calculation, collaboration, and file-processing features in products and agent experiences.
sections.why_notable: Its growth points to interest in embedding spreadsheet and office capabilities into products and agent workflows.

sections.title: backnotprop/plannotator
sections.description: A local review workspace for annotating agent plans, artifacts, and code changes, with feedback routed back to the agent.
sections.content: The README describes a local browser-based review surface for plans, specs, HTML artifacts, agent messages, diffs, and pull requests, with comments returned to supported agent sessions.
sections.why_notable: It makes human review a first-class feedback loop across multiple coding agents.
sections.unique_caveat: It is a review and integration layer for agents rather than a standalone coding agent.

sections.title: martin-olivier/airgorah
sections.why_notable: A security-focused counterpoint to the agent-heavy projects, with a notable daily gain.
sections.unique_caveat: The API snapshot showed the default branch had not been pushed since 2026-11-06, despite today's displayed star gain.

sections.title: QwenLM/qwen-code
sections.description: An open-source coding agent that spans terminal, editor, desktop, browser, and chat interfaces.
sections.content: The README describes an agent harness with skills, memory, subagents, MCP, multiple model-provider protocols, and several user interfaces.
sections.why_notable: It represents the broadening of coding agents from terminal programs into multiple interfaces and model-provider ecosystems.
sections.unique_caveat: The README distinguishes the main release from a separate 1.0 Preview branch; capabilities and installation paths may vary by version.

sections.title: Tencent/LoopForge
sections.description: Self-hosted workflows for delivering code with coding agents and human approval gates.
sections.content: The Trending description identifies workflows coordinating CodeBuddy, Codex, and Claude Code with scripts and human approval gates.
sections.why_notable: It makes agent orchestration and explicit human approval part of the delivery pipeline.
sections.unique_caveat: This snapshot's detail is based on the short Trending description and API metadata; README workflow specifics were not separately checked.

sections.title: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui
sections.description: A protocol for connecting agents to frontend applications.
sections.content: The project describes a protocol for connecting agent systems to frontend applications.
sections.why_notable: It represents protocol-level integration work alongside end-user agent products, though its displayed daily gain is modest.
sections.unique_caveat: The displayed daily gain is modest relative to the rest of this set.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent guidance and review: Modern Web Guidance supplies current browser expertise to agents; OpenCodeReview combines deterministic review steps with LLM reasoning; Plannotator routes human annotations to agents. Browser access and agent integration: Chrome DevTools MCP provides live browser automation and diagnostics, Qwen Code spans multiple interfaces, and AG-UI targets the agent-to-frontend boundary. Workflow orchestration and domain skills: LoopForge adds approval-gated delivery and Claude Trading Skills specializes agent-driven market workflows. Beyond agents, Sure and Univer indicate finance and office-productivity interest, while Airgorah adds Wi-Fi security auditing. Languages: TypeScript 6/11, Go 2/11, Python 1/11, Ruby 1/11, Rust 1/11.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The strongest shared signal is the infrastructure around agents: current domain guidance, browser access, code review, feedback loops, and approval-gated delivery. At the same time, the daily list rewards concrete user-facing products and security tools too. Daily star gains indicate short-window attention, not by themselves lasting adoption or project quality.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily, captured 2026-11-14 17:35 UTC. Corroboration: GitHub Search query pushed:2026-11-12..2026-11-14 stars:>100 fork:false sorted by stars; REST repo and default-branch commit endpoints checked for all 11 listed projects. Five high-priority current READMEs were read. Daily gains come from the official Trending page; no prior-window comparison was available.
